|-------|------------|

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.

TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.

aiTitle: Design scalable agent discovery and organization system

content.thinking:
The user wants to build a dynamic, scalable agent directory/org chart system that can handle 100+ agents across different domains (Shopify, Figma, WordPress, video editing, sales, etc.). They want:

1. A way to easily find the right agent for the right task
2. Visual filtering by technology/domain (Shopify, Figma, WordPress, etc.)
3. Multiple view options
4. Scalable to 100+ agents
5. Something that shows agents grouped by work type (e.g., "Figma design work", "Shopify work", "WordPress work")


I'm thinking through the core problem here—they need a way to organize and discover agents across multiple dimensions like technology, work type, and department. I could approach this with a tag-based filtering system, an interactive HTML interface, or a CLI tool that lets them search and filter agents dynamically.

The best path forward seems to be building a metadata system that powers both a visual dashboard and command-line queries, so they get flexibility in how they interact with the agent directory. I'd add structured tags to each agent, then create multiple views—an org chart, a tech stack view, a work type view—all filterable and searchable to handle scaling to 100+ agents.

Now I need to explore the actual structure of their agents and registry to understand what I'm working with, then design the metadata schema and dashboard accordingly. Let me look at the existing agent structure to understand what fields are already there and what I need to add.

## What I Found in the Codebase

The system is a Node.js/Express backend (`src/`) with a vanilla HTML frontend (`public/index.html`). Data lives in two JSON files: `~/.claude/org/registry.json` (source of truth for agent metadata) and `~/.claude/org/departments.json` (department/phase definitions). The `upsertAgent(id, patch)` function in `src/org.js` uses spread-merge, so adding a `tags` field to registry entries is strictly non-destructive. The existing `PATCH /api/org/agent/:id` endpoint has a hardcoded `allowed` array that currently excludes `tags` — that is the one line that must change. The `buildOrgChart()` function in `src/org.js` already computes per-agent nodes; extending it to pass-through `tags` requires one line. No database schema changes are needed (SQLite is only used for runs/events, not agent records).

The existing public dashboard at `public/index.html` uses a clean design system: CSS custom properties, DM Sans font, sidebar + main panel layout, light/dark mode, `--accent #2D5BE3`, semantic color tokens. The new HTML dashboard should inherit this exact design language.

## Part 3: Registry.json Enhancement

The `tags` field is an object with three arrays. It is additive — existing keys are untouched.

```json
"tags": {
  "tech": ["shopify", "react", "typescript"],
  "domain": ["ecommerce", "saas"],
  "work-type": ["coding"]
}
```

The `upsertAgent()` function already uses spread-merge `{ ...existing, ...patch }`, so writing `tags` to any agent will not touch any other field. No migration script is needed — just a one-time seed pass. The registry's `version` field should bump from `1` to `2` after tag seeding.

### PATCH endpoint change (one line in `src/routes/orgHr.js` line ~106)

The `allowed` array must add `'tags'`:

```js
const allowed = [
  'department', 'subDepartment', 'pod', 'phase', 'reportsTo',
  'secondaryReportsTo', 'title', 'tier', 'status', 'tags'   // <-- add tags
];
```

Additionally, a new read endpoint should be added to `src/routes/orgHr.js`:

```
GET /api/agents/directory
  ?tech=shopify          (comma-sep, any match)
  ?domain=ecommerce
  ?work-type=coding
  ?department=engineering
  ?tier=engineer|leadership|analyst|creative
  ?q=search-term         (name/title/description fuzzy)
```

This endpoint merges registry records with frontmatter-parsed agent data from disk, applies filters, and returns a flat array sorted by department order then agent id.


# Agent Discovery & Directory System — Complete Design Plan

## What I Found in the Codebase

The system is a Node.js/Express backend (`src/`) with a vanilla HTML frontend (`public/index.html`). Data lives in two JSON files: `~/.claude/org/registry.json` (source of truth for agent metadata) and `~/.claude/org/departments.json` (department/phase definitions). The `upsertAgent(id, patch)` function in `src/org.js` uses spread-merge, so adding a `tags` field to registry entries is strictly non-destructive. The existing `PATCH /api/org/agent/:id` endpoint has a hardcoded `allowed` array that currently excludes `tags` — that is the one line that must change. The `buildOrgChart()` function in `src/org.js` already computes per-agent nodes; extending it to pass-through `tags` requires one line. No database schema changes are needed (SQLite is only used for runs/events, not agent records).

The existing public dashboard at `public/index.html` uses a clean design system: CSS custom properties, DM Sans font, sidebar + main panel layout, light/dark mode, `--accent #2D5BE3`, semantic color tokens. The new HTML dashboard should inherit this exact design language.

---

## Part 1: Tag Taxonomy (38 tags across 3 categories)

| `react` | React component work (not framework-specific) |

| `railway` | Railway deployment/infra |
| `figma` | Figma MCP tools, .fig files, Code Connect |

| `tailwind` | Tailwind CSS / design tokens |

| `posthog` | Analytics / PostHog integration |

### Category B: `domain` — Business domain tags (11 tags)

## Part 3: Registry.json Enhancement

The `tags` field is an object with three arrays. It is additive — existing keys are untouched.

```json
"tags": {
  "tech": ["shopify", "react", "typescript"],
  "domain": ["ecommerce", "saas"],
  "work-type": ["coding"]

```

The `upsertAgent()` function already uses spread-merge `{ ...existing, ...patch }`, so writing `tags` to any agent will not touch any other field. No migration script is needed — just a one-time seed pass. The registry's `version` field should bump from `1` to `2` after tag seeding.

### PATCH endpoint change (one line in `src/routes/orgHr.js` line ~106)

The `allowed` array must add `'tags'`:

```js
const allowed = [
  'department', 'subDepartment', 'pod', 'phase', 'reportsTo',
  'secondaryReportsTo', 'title', 'tier', 'status', 'tags'   // <-- add tags
];
```

Additionally, a new read endpoint should be added to `src/routes/orgHr.js`:

```
GET /api/agents/directory
  ?tech=shopify          (comma-sep, any match)
  ?domain=ecommerce
  ?work-type=coding
  ?department=engineering
  ?tier=engineer|leadership|analyst|creative
  ?q=search-term         (name/title/description fuzzy)
```

This endpoint merges registry records with frontmatter-parsed agent data from disk, applies filters, and returns a flat array sorted by department order then agent id.

### Design System (inherits from `public/index.html`)

```css
/* Inherit from public/index.html exactly */
--bg: #F8F7F4 / #161615 (dark)
--bg2: #FFFFFF / #1E1E1C

--tag-work-type: #4A1E6E / #C4B5FD  (purple — coding, design, testing)
```

### Tag Pills Color System

- `tech` tags: blue background (`--accent-bg`) with blue text (`--accent-tx`)
- `domain` tags: green background (`--green-bg`) with green text (`--green`)
- `work-type` tags: purple background (`--purple-bg`) with purple text (`--purple`)

Each tag is clickable and acts as a toggle filter.

### Layout: Left Sidebar + Right Content Panel

```
[Sidebar 240px fixed]      [Content area flex-1]
  Logo + agent count         [Header bar with search + view toggle]
  ─ FILTER BY TECH           [Active filter chips row]
    [ ] shopify  (12)          ✕ shopify  ✕ coding
    [ ] figma    (5)
```

Cards in `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(280px, 1fr))`. Each card shows:

- Title + department badge
- One-line description (clamped to 2 lines)

- Add `'tags'` to the `allowed` array in `PATCH /api/org/agent/:id` (~line 106)

```bash
# Examples:
```

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/orgHr.js`
- `~/.claude/org/tag-taxonomy.json` — new
- `~/.claude/org/directory.html` — new dashboard
- `~/.claude/org/scripts/find-agents.sh` — new CLI

  ReactFlow,
  Background,

  Users, Search, Cpu, Paintbrush, BarChart3, Shield,

import type { Agent } from '../types'
import LevelBadge, { levelColors } from '../components/LevelBadge'
import AgentIcon from '../components/AgentIcon'

// ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// Department view constants
const DEPT_WIDTH = 340
const DEPT_HEADER_HEIGHT = 68
const DEPT_PADDING_Y = 14
const MEMBER_ROW_HEIGHT = 90
const MEMBER_ROW_GAP = 6
const DEPT_ROW_GAP = 36
const LEADER_WIDTH = 260
const LEADER_HEIGHT = 118
const LEADER_DEPT_GAP = 28
// Multi-level tree gaps:
//   Row 0 (Rex)         → Row 1 (dept heads): DEPT_HEAD_ROW_GAP
//   Row 1 (dept heads)  → Row 2 (dept cols):  LEADER_DEPT_GAP (existing)
const DEPT_HEAD_ROW_GAP = 60
// Sub-member indent inside a department column (L3+ reports under a sub-manager)
const SUB_MEMBER_INDENT = 14

// Org Structure v2 — sub-department group header height inside a dept column
const SUBDEPT_HEADER_HEIGHT = 30
const SUBDEPT_HEADER_GAP = 4

// Context for selecting a member from inside a DepartmentNode
// (avoids passing callbacks through node.data which causes re-render churn)
const OrgSelectContext = createContext<{
  selectedId: string | null
  onSelect: (id: string) => void
}>({ selectedId: null, onSelect: () => {} })


const TIER_ICONS: Record<string, typeof Cpu> = {
  leadership: Shield,
  engineer: Cpu,
  analyst: BarChart3,

}

const MODEL_BADGES: Record<string, { label: string; bg: string; text: string; border: string }> = {

  haiku: { label: 'Haiku', bg: 'rgba(52,211,153,0.15)', text: '#34d399', border: 'rgba(52,211,153,0.3)' },
}

function extractEmoji(name: string): { emoji: string; cleanName: string } {
  const emoji = name.match(/^(\p{Emoji_Presentation}|\p{Extended_Pictographic})/u)?.[0] || ''
  const cleanName = name
    .replace(/^[\p{Emoji_Presentation}\p{Extended_Pictographic}]\s*[\u200d\ufe0f]*/u, '')
    .replace(/^—\s*/, '')
    .trim()
  return { emoji, cleanName: cleanName.split('—')[0]?.trim() || cleanName }
}

// ── Department Layout Algorithm ──────────────────────────────────────────────

interface MemberInfo {
  id: string
  name: string
  emoji: string
  title: string
  model: string
  tier: string
  phaseColor: string

  // Indent depth inside a department column. 0 = direct report of the dept head;

  // Org Structure v2 — sub-department + pod for grouping inside dept column
  subDepartment?: string | null
  subDepartmentLabel?: string | null
  pod?: string | null
  secondaryReportsTo?: string | null
}

// Org Structure v2 — sub-department group inside a dept column
interface SubDeptGroup {
  id: string
  label: string
  description: string
  pod: string | null
  members: MemberInfo[]
}

# Agent Discovery & Directory System

## Context
42 agents today → 100+ soon. Current org chart is unnavigable. No way to filter "all Shopify agents" or "all Figma design agents". Need a tag system + visual dashboard + CLI query tool that scales without confusion.

---

## Tag Taxonomy (38 tags, 3 categories)

**Tech** (blue pills): `shopify` `nextjs` `supabase` `react` `typescript` `railway` `figma` `playwright` `tailwind` `polaris` `hydrogen` `postgresql` `shadcn` `postmark` `sentry` `posthog`

**Domain** (green pills): `ecommerce` `saas` `design-system` `devops` `data` `seo` `conversion` `market-research` `portfolio` `hr-ops` `brand`

**Work-type** (purple pills): `design` `coding` `testing` `copywriting` `email` `strategy` `research` `review` `deploy` `training` `monitoring`

---

## Tag Assignment (all 42 agents)

| Agent | Tech | Domain | Work-type |
|-------|------|--------|-----------|
| rex | nextjs, shopify, supabase | saas, ecommerce, portfolio | strategy |
| arya | nextjs, shopify, supabase, react, typescript | saas, ecommerce, data | strategy, coding |

| sage | nextjs, shopify, supabase, react, typescript | saas, ecommerce | review, testing |
| koda | nextjs, supabase, react, typescript, shadcn, tailwind | saas | coding |
| dato | supabase, postgresql | data | coding |
| riko | nextjs, supabase, react, typescript, railway, tailwind, shadcn | saas, devops | coding |
| pod-b-frontend | shopify, polaris, react, typescript | ecommerce | coding |
| pod-b-backend | shopify, postgresql | ecommerce, data | coding |
| pod-b-db | shopify, postgresql | ecommerce, data | coding |
| pod-b-tester | shopify, playwright | ecommerce | testing |
| bolt | nextjs, shopify, railway, supabase | saas, ecommerce, devops | deploy |
| hawk | railway, sentry, posthog | saas, ecommerce, devops | monitoring |
| luna | nextjs, shopify, supabase, playwright, typescript | saas, ecommerce | testing |
| vega | figma, tailwind, shadcn, polaris | saas, ecommerce, design-system | design, strategy |
| pixel | nextjs, tailwind, shadcn | saas | design |
| elio | figma, tailwind | ecommerce, brand | design |
| token | figma, tailwind, shadcn, polaris | design-system, saas, ecommerce | design |
| figma-synth | figma, react, typescript | design-system, ecommerce, saas | design |
| quill | _(none)_ | saas, ecommerce, brand | copywriting |
| spark | _(none)_ | ecommerce, conversion, brand | copywriting |
| merch | _(none)_ | ecommerce, brand | copywriting |
| zeph | nextjs, shopify | saas, ecommerce, seo | coding, strategy |
| sequence | postmark | ecommerce | email, copywriting |
| echo | _(none)_ | saas, ecommerce, portfolio | strategy |
| catalyst | _(none)_ | ecommerce, conversion | strategy |
| ecom-cro | shopify | ecommerce, conversion | strategy, coding |
| decoder | figma | ecommerce, brand, conversion | research |
| harvest | _(none)_ | market-research | research |
| nova | shopify | saas, ecommerce, market-research, portfolio | research, strategy |
| scout | _(none)_ | saas, ecommerce, portfolio | research |
| atlas | _(none)_ | saas, ecommerce, market-research, portfolio | research |
| ledger | _(none)_ | saas, ecommerce, portfolio | research |
| orbit | posthog | saas, ecommerce, portfolio | research, strategy |
| pulse | _(none)_ | saas, ecommerce, market-research | research |
| verdict | _(none)_ | saas, ecommerce, portfolio | strategy |
| cadence | _(none)_ | hr-ops | strategy |
| forge | _(none)_ | hr-ops | strategy, coding |
| tutor | _(none)_ | hr-ops | training |
| mira | _(none)_ | hr-ops | training |
| witness | supabase | hr-ops | monitoring |
| roster | supabase | hr-ops, data | strategy |

---

## What Gets Built

### 1. `~/.claude/org/tag-taxonomy.json`
Machine-readable tag list (category, description, color). Used by dashboard + CLI + Forge on new hires.

### 2. `~/.claude/org/registry.json` — tag seed
Add `"tags": { "tech": [...], "domain": [...], "work-type": [...] }` to all 42 agent entries. Existing fields untouched. Version bump `1 → 2`.

### 3. `src/org.js` — 2 changes (~25 lines)
- Add `tags: record.tags || {}` to the agent node object inside `buildOrgChart()`
- Add `findAgentsByTags(tagQuery)` utility function (AND across categories, OR within)

### 4. `src/routes/orgHr.js` — 2 changes (~40 lines)
- Add `'tags'` to the `allowed` array in `PATCH /api/org/agent/:id` (~line 106)
- Add new endpoint `GET /api/agents/directory` with query params: `?tech=shopify&domain=ecommerce&work-type=coding&department=engineering&q=search`

### 5. `~/.claude/org/directory.html` — standalone dashboard
Self-contained HTML/CSS/JS (~600 lines). Fetches `GET /api/agents/directory`.

**Views (4 toggleable):**
- **Grid** — auto-fill cards, grouped flat
- **List** — sortable table
- **By Department** — collapsible dept sections
- **By Tech Stack** — one section per tech tag; agents appear in multiple sections

**Filter sidebar:**
- Checkboxes per tag (count shown next to each)
- AND logic across categories, OR within category
- Live search (name/title/description, 100ms debounce)
- Active filter chips row with ✕ to remove

**Agent card shows:**
- Emoji + name + level badge + model badge (opus=amber, sonnet=blue, haiku=gray)
- Title + department
- 2-line description clamp
- Tech pills (blue), domain pills (green), work-type pills (purple) — max 4+2+2 shown
- Reports-to chain

**Slide-out panel on click:** full tags, full description, skills scorecard, same-pod strip, shared-tech-stack strip.

### 6. `~/.claude/org/scripts/find-agents.sh` — CLI query (~100 lines)

```bash
# Examples:
./find-agents.sh --tech shopify
./find-agents.sh --tech figma --work-type design
./find-agents.sh --domain ecommerce --work-type testing
./find-agents.sh --department engineering
./find-agents.sh --q "bug"
./find-agents.sh --list-tags
./find-agents.sh --tech shopify --json   # raw JSON output
```

Reads `~/.claude/org/registry.json` directly via `node -e` or `python3 -c`. Outputs formatted table. No server required.

---

## Filter Logic
- Multiple selected within same category = **OR**
- Across categories = **AND**
- Example: `tech=[shopify,figma]` + `work-type=[design]` → agents with (shopify OR figma) AND design

---

## Implementation Order

1. `tag-taxonomy.json` — no deps
2. `registry.json` tag seed — all 42 agents
3. `src/org.js` — pass-through + utility fn
4. `src/routes/orgHr.js` — PATCH + GET endpoint
5. `directory.html` — against live API
6. `find-agents.sh` — reads registry.json directly

---

## Verification

1. `./find-agents.sh --tech shopify` → shows all Shopify agents in table
2. `./find-agents.sh --tech figma --work-type design` → elio, token, figma-synth, vega
3. Open `directory.html` in browser → filter sidebar works, 4 view modes toggle, cards load
4. Tech Stack view → "shopify" section shows 12+ agents, "figma" section shows ~5
5. Agent card click → slide-out shows same-pod strip + shared-tech strip
6. `PATCH /api/org/agent/koda` with `{ "tags": {...} }` → 200 OK

---

## Critical File Paths

- `~/.claude/org/registry.json` — tag seed target
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/org.js`
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Operation/Polyglot/src/routes/orgHr.js`
- `~/.claude/org/tag-taxonomy.json` — new
- `~/.claude/org/directory.html` — new dashboard
- `~/.claude/org/scripts/find-agents.sh` — new CLI

content.text:
Build clean. Done.

**What changed in filter panel:**

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| 4 rows always visible | 2 rows always visible + 1 collapsed |
| 43 pills total | 18 pills default, +12 expandable |
| Squad + Tech + Domain + Work | Squad + Work + (`+ Tech filters` toggle) |
| Domain row (redundant w/ squad) | **Removed** |
| Tech row (14 pills incl. rare ones) | Trimmed to 12, hidden behind toggle |
| `hydrogen sentry posthog postmark` | Dropped (1-agent-each tags) |

**Now:**
- Click `Filter` → see Squad pills (7) + Work pills (11)
- Need tech granularity? Click `+ Tech filters` → row expands
- Active count badge counts only squad+tech+work (no domain)
- Registry data preserved — domain tags still queryable via CLI `--domain` and API `?domain=` for power users
